findings.reason: the node must be told the stream (stderr) and the parser contract (stdout stays one JSON document) or the call site added to the write paths, otherwise it implements the print where the plan says and breaks two shipped callers that no listed case measures.
findings.text: the Deliverable requires the pass to print "its progress and per-phase timing as it goes", but the two real callers both emit one JSON document on stdout — `main()` writes `json.dumps(report, indent=2)` to stdout (reckon/crew/gc.py:1736) and the `crew retention-sweep` verb emits the same report through `_emit_crew_result` (reckon/crew_run_commands.py:1814) — so a pass that prints inside `retention_sweep` corrupts the JSON envelope of both, and the plan's write paths (`reckon/crew/gc.py`, the new test, the fragment) exclude the CLI call site where that would be repaired

findings.reason: without a cursor-only control the node can ship the resumed-cursor claim on a case that its own control never exercises, and the earlier review's finding is answered on paper only.
findings.text: the declared negative control is "counts only offered rows again, and the first case fails", which falsifies the judged-limit change alone; the second case (300 withheld directories passed by the fourth pass) is proved only by the cursor, and no stated control reverts the cursor to show that case reddens

findings.reason: a node can satisfy every listed case and the five-minute bound while the per-directory config resolution survives, so the clause that names the phase's real cost has nothing that reddens when it is left in place.
findings.text: the Deliverable requires "each phase reads its inputs once per pass", but none of the four cases and neither host run measures it: the concrete target is `_run_directory_grace_seconds` (reckon/crew/gc.py:1467-1548), which resolves the flight config through `flight.resolve(project, checkout_path=root)` once per judged directory inside the loop
